entry.title: Peter Zumthor unveils trio of “wonderfully expressive” buildings for Swiss museum

media:group.media:title: Peter Zumthor unveils trio of “wonderfully expressive” buildings for Swiss museum
media:group.media:description:
Swiss architect Peter Zumthor has expanded the Fondation Beyeler museum in Riehen, Switzerland, with a cluster of art buildings designed to nestle into the park setting.
Built in the gardens outside the original Fondation Beyeler art museum, which was designed by Renzo Piano in 1997, the trio of buildings include a rammed-concrete art gallery, a glazed cultural space and a wood-clad office building.
Find out more on dezeen.com

entry.title: "Things start in really simple gestures" says Es Devlin of her Design Museum retrospective

media:group.media:title: "Things start in really simple gestures" says Es Devlin of her Design Museum retrospective
media:group.media:description:
British artist and designer Es Devlin explains how ambitious creative projects begin with simple ideas in an exclusive video interview with Dezeen, filmed at Other Worlds, her first European retrospective at London's Design Museum.
Named Other Worlds, the retrospective brings together three decades of Devlin's work across theatre, opera, concert stage design and large-scale public installations.
The exhibition explores how Devlin's projects develop, from early drawings and models to monumental installations experienced by audiences around the world.
In the interview, she explains how she hopes the presentation will demystify the creative process and encourage visitors to pursue their own ideas.
Find out more on dezeen.com

media:group.media:title: Tuesday Labs debuts “droid butler” Voxel
media:group.media:description:
New York technology company Tuesday Labs has debuted its first semi-autonomous robot Voxel Series-1, designed to help with household chores and to avoid the appearance of an “uncanny valley” humanoid robot.
Voxel Series-1 (Voxel) performs tasks such as watering plants and sweeping crumbs, which it currently achieves with a combination of autonomous intelligence and teleoperation.
The robot is counter-height and covered in a colourful matte plastic shell with primarily “cuboid” body parts, LED eyes and 1-DOF grippers for hands. Tuesday Labs founder Rosalind Shinkle told Dezeen that initial designs were informed by home objects such as lamps, chairs and briefcases.
Read more on Dezeen: http://www.dezeen.com/?p=2377182

entry.title: Andy Matthews designs Dulwich cricket pavilion to be antithesis of "off-the-shelf generic designs"

media:group.media:title: Andy Matthews designs Dulwich cricket pavilion to be antithesis of "off-the-shelf generic designs"
media:group.media:description:
Architecture practice Andy Matthews Studio has unveiled a black, contemporary cricket pavilion on Dulwich Common, south London.
Built for Streatham & Marlborough Cricket Club, the pavilion stands alongside Dulwich Common overlooking the club's main pitch.
The mono-pitch main form was designed to be a contemporary expression of a traditional cricket pavilion, while demonstrating the quality of facilities possible for community sports clubs.
Read more on Dezeen: https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2373190

entry.title: Jaguar "inaugurates a new era" with Type 01 electric car

media:group.media:title: Jaguar "inaugurates a new era" with Type 01 electric car
media:group.media:description:
Dezeen's Tom Ravenscroft took an exclusive look at the much-anticipated electric car at the Jaguar's flagship store in London.
Created as the first car in a "complete reset" for the brand, the car has a highly distinctive form with an elongated bonnet and two sets of thin headlights on its grille. It is 5.2 metres long and only 1.4 metres high. With a rear-leaning stance that evokes heritage Jaguar models, the car has an aluminium body. Its rear-quarter panel was pressed five times, leading to Jaguar dubbing it the "impossible panel".
Find out more on Dezeen.com
📸 Simon Volt

entry.title: Bar Shrimp uses laser-etched acoustic panels to balance music and conversation

media:group.media:title: Bar Shrimp uses laser-etched acoustic panels to balance music and conversation
media:group.media:description:
Manchester cocktail bar and restaurant Bar Shrimp combines red velvet interiors with bespoke acoustic panels from Autex Acoustics to balance music and conversation, shown in this video produced by Dezeen.
Located in Manchester, Bar Shrimp has a dark interior with floor-to-ceiling red velvet curtains, plush banquettes and a custom sound system, reminiscent of vintage New York bars and music lounges.
The design was informed by the founders' experience of bars around the world, where co-founder Richard Cossins said they were struck by spaces with particularly good sound.

entry.title: David Chipperfield Architects celebrates two of its "most important projects" in short film

media:group.media:title: David Chipperfield Architects celebrates two of its "most important projects" in short film
media:group.media:description:
British studio David Chipperfield Architects celebrates 15 years of the Hepworth Wakefield and Turner Contemporary in this short film, shared here exclusively with Dezeen.
Opened within weeks of each other, the Hepworth Wakefield gallery in West Yorkshire and the Turner Contemporary museum in Margate are considered two of the studio's most important projects, influencing the evolution of its work that followed.
To mark their 15-year anniversary, David Chipperfield Architects is publishing this short film exclusively with Dezeen, which documents the success of the projects through insights from people who work at and frequent the galleries.

entry.title: Harvard University transforms waste wool into cladding for retrofits

media:group.media:title: Harvard University transforms waste wool into cladding for retrofits
media:group.media:description:
Grinham Research Group at Harvard University has developed an insulating cladding tile made from waste wool, which was presented at this year's Oslo Architecture Triennale.
In an installation named Upcycling Wool Ecologies, Grinham Research Group showcased its tiles on a timber frame in Oslo's Sofienberg Church as part of the triennale's main exhibition, which takes place from 17 September to 1 October.
Grinham Research Group saw the potential in wool's insulative, fire-resistant and antibacterial properties, and wanted to save it from being discarded as a residual material in the agricultural and textile industries.
The group also wanted to develop a material that could help facilitate building reuse.
The video is by Grinham Research Group.
Read more at: https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2367975

entry.title: "Where is design headed?" Reece Davey interviews Dezeen Awards 2026 master jury

media:group.media:title: "Where is design headed?" Reece Davey interviews Dezeen Awards 2026 master jury
media:group.media:description:
Where is design headed? Content creator Reece Davey (houseofdvey) went straight to the source...
Last week, Davey sat in on the Dezeen Awards master jury, sponsored by Trimble, and cornered some of the world's leading architects and designers between deliberations to ask one big question: what does the future of architecture and design actually look like?!
Emotion and colour are back. Ornament is no longer a dirty word! Buildings designed for the climate of 2076, not 2026... And the tools are moving fast: sketch it, model it, visualise it in Trimble SketchUp, and iterate your way to an award-worthy idea in minutes rather than months!
Your turn! Where is design going? Tell us in the comments!
Dezeen Awards 2026 shortlists drop Monday 21 September on dezeen.com... set an alarm!
Video produced by Reece Davey in collaboration with Dezeen Studio

entry.title: Richard and Su Roger's 22 Parkside acquired by the National Trust

media:group.media:title: Richard and Su Roger's 22 Parkside acquired by the National Trust
media:group.media:description:
Architecture reporter Amy Peacock takes a look inside modernist icon 22 Parkside, which was recently announced as acquired by the National Trust.
The home was designed by architects Richard and Su Rogers, who created the house for Richard's parents.
The one-storey building was a testing ground for Rogers, serving as a "miniature prototype" for the Centre Pompidou in Paris, and helping shape the design of his later works, such as the Lloyd’s building in London.
22 Parkside is located in Wimbledon, London, and will be fully open to the public from 2028 - although select viewings are planned ahead of then.
Video produced and edited by Francesca Tesler.

entry.title: Tod Williams Billie Tsien Architects completes "intentionally sculptural" Obama Presidential Center

media:group.media:title: Tod Williams Billie Tsien Architects completes "intentionally sculptural" Obama Presidential Center
media:group.media:description:
A monumental granite-clad tower surrounded by artificial hills has been completed by US studio Tod Williams Billie Tsien Architects to honour US president Barack Obama.
Ten years after Barack Obama left office, the Obama Presidential Center will open to visitors next week in Chicago's South Side.

entry.title: “Water reed serves a really important in our hydrological landscape” says Alys Hargreaves

media:group.media:title: “Water reed serves a really important in our hydrological landscape” says Alys Hargreaves
media:group.media:description:
Earlier this month, Dezeen’s architecture reporter Amy Peacock caught up with architectural designer Alys Hargreaves from Cella Collective at Houghton Festival.
Cella Collective, in collaboration with Mitre & Mondays, unveiled a new monumental timber-and-thatch pavilion on the festival grounds. The structure was informed by Houghton Hall’s historic 1772 water tower and was constructed using sustainably harvested reed from Scottish RSPB reedbeds, highlighting how regenerative design can support biodiversity and traditional craft.
Peacock and Hargreaves also discuss why materiality matters, how design plays a part in the festival experience, and other must-see installations at this year’s Houghton Festival such as wooden thrones by Call Super.
🎥 by Simon Volt
Houghton Minute is a Dezeen video produced with Houghton Festival

entry.title: Gamers must survive without air-con in Europe Heatwave Simulator

media:group.media:title: Gamers must survive without air-con in Europe Heatwave Simulator
media:group.media:description:
Game developer Blue Hood Games has released a survival game named Europe Heatwave Simulator, where players need to outlast a 14-day heatwave without air conditioning in an apartment in Paris.
Playable on the Steam platform, which is downloadable for Windows desktops, Europe Heatwave Simulator challenges players to survive a fortnight in a Parisian apartment in 42-degree Celsius heat.
In the game, players navigate life without air conditioning, tending to the needs of their overheating body by keeping cool, hydrated and fed, while also working a remote job from a laptop on the dining table.
Blue Hood Games described Europe Heatwave Simulator as a "dark humour" game centred on "the crushing reality of modern European summers without air conditioning".
Read more: https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2355089
